title: Lossy Compression with Intent Alignment — rich
forward_vector: I am the manifest of Lossy Compression with Intent Alignment's rich face, its first round, at Sketch tier, a proposal. For the rate-distortion-perception tradeoff: a cymbal made in the page, coded at a fixed rate and decoded two ways from the same bits, the least-error average and a draw, walked up from one sample at fewer bits to a blind test of your ear against the error meter; and the same for the eye, on four textures. For soft labels: the page's own link to Resonant Link Labels, typed then labelled, the palace's links counted, what distillation means by soft, and sixteen real links to rebuild from the type or the label. Every blind test states its chance and its rule first. The memory, the deposit and the cross-domain sections have nothing a piece could test, so they have nothing. I grow when a reader's results come back. I never hold the entry's words.

pieces.file: Lossy Compression with Intent Alignment — rich — same bits, two decoders.html
pieces.title: Same bits, two decoders · from one sample at fewer bits to a blind test of ear against meter
pieces.caption: **Does the decoding with the least error sound like the original?** Five steps, one synthetic cymbal (square waves at inharmonic pitches and seeded noise; no sample, no recording). Each sample at fewer bits, and the error that leaves. A transform coder at 32 kbps: 341 bits a frame, 125 of them band levels, 78 % of coefficients given no bits. What a decoder writes where the bits ran out: the cell’s average, the least error, or a draw from the cell; the draw’s error is twice the average’s, 2.00 measured, the theorem’s number. The three axes at 32, 64 and 128 kbps, on the cymbal and on a held tone where the effect is smaller; the draw needs about 67 kbps to reach the average’s error at 32. Last, eight blind trials of the two decodings of the same bits, matched in K-weighted loudness, against the original. The rule is stated before the first: 7 or 8 of 8 for one decoder happens by guessing about 1 time in 28. Noise is where the effect is largest; a tone shows less of it.

pieces.file: Lossy Compression with Intent Alignment — rich — same bits, two pictures.html
pieces.title: Same bits, two pictures · the tradeoff for the eye, blind
pieces.caption: **The same claim, seen.** Four textures made from seeded noise; a block coder at 0.35, 0.5 or 1 bit a pixel against the original’s 8. The average of each cell gives the least error and a smoother picture; a draw from each cell gives the grain back and about 3 dB less PSNR, an error 1.77 to 2.14 times the average’s. Then eight blind pairs, four textures at two rates, sides at random: which is more like the original? Same rule, stated first: 7 or 8 of 8 for one decoder is about 1 time in 28 by guessing. Every number is worked out from the pictures’ own values, never read off the screen.
pieces.near: A faithful summary has low distortion

pieces.file: Lossy Compression with Intent Alignment — rich — the type and the label.html
pieces.title: The type and the label · sixteen of the palace’s links, rebuilt
pieces.caption: **Does a link’s label let you rebuild it where its type can’t?** Four steps on the palace’s own links. This page’s link to Resonant Link Labels as the type says it, spawned, one of 107 of 2,087 links; then with its label, midwifed, one of 2. What distillation means by a soft label, a spread over the same classes, and how rarely a palace label is one: 28 of 1,600 labels sit under more than one type. Last, sixteen real links from sixteen pages, eight shown with the type alone and eight with the label too, each with four of the source’s real targets: pick the right one. Chance is 1 in 4; 5 or more of 8 in an arm happens by guessing about 1 time in 37. Labels that spell their target were left out of the pool. Counts as at commit 3bd902d3; the check recounts.
pieces.near: Applied to the palace: the typed links

offers.what: The section defines Perception as how well the compressed version functions for its intended receiver. In the 2019 framework (Blau and Michaeli) it is narrower: how far the distribution of decoded outputs sits from the distribution of real ones, whether a decoding looks or sounds like a real sample, with no receiver’s purpose in it; serving a purpose is closer to task-oriented or semantic compression. The pieces test the narrow sense and the tradeoff holds there. Suggest naming both: the theory’s perception, and the palace’s reading of it as fitness for the receiver.

The section says high perception costs more, and reads the cost as deliberate work. The theory prices it in bits or in error, and the pieces measured both: at the same bits the draw’s error is 2.00 times the least error on the synthetic cymbal at every rate from 16 to 128 kbps (1.77 to 2.14 on four synthetic textures), and the draw needs about 67 kbps, 2.09 times the bits, to reach the average’s error at 32 kbps. Suggest the text say the price is paid in bits or in error, and keep deliberate work as the palace’s reading of it.

In distillation a soft label is a spread of probability over the same classes the hard label picks from; its signal is in what the wrong classes get. A palace label is a finer name, not a spread: of 1,600 labels on 2,087 entry-to-entry links (commit 3bd902d3), 1,517 are used once and 28 appear under more than one type; midwifed sits wholly in spawned. A label does carry more specificity (a type alone 2.51 bits on average, type and label 10.70), so “more signal than the hard type” holds in that sense; “soft” is the wrong word for it. Suggest “finer label” or “named register”, or say where the analogy holds and where it doesn’t.

The paragraph says “the typed links between entries are soft labels”, then calls a type, enables, a hard label. It means the label a typed link carries. Suggest: “the labels on the palace’s typed links are soft labels”.
